questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT a superkey in a relational schema with attributes
V,W, X, Y, Z and primary key V Y?
questions.solution:
A superkey must contain the whole primary key {V, Y}.
VWXZ has V but no Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not a superkey. The others all contain both V and Y.

Answer: VWXZ

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the ACID properties of database transactions?
questions.solution:
ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. Deadlock-freedom is not one of them.

Answer: Deadlock-freedom

questions.text:
A database of resear charticles in a journal uses the following schema.

Which is the weakest normal form that the new database satisfies,but the old one does not?
questions.solution:
Old schema: key (VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE), and (VOLUME, NUMBER) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] YEAR is a partial dependency (part of the key determines a non-key attribute) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] only 1NF.

New schemas: YEAR moves to (VOLUME, NUMBER, YEAR), so the partial dependency is gone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2NF (in fact both are in BCNF).

The weakest form the new one satisfies but the old one does not is 2NF.

Answer: 2NF

questions.text: Which one of the following protocols is NOT used to resolve one form of address to another one?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- DNS: hostname [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IP
- ARP: IP [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] MAC
- RARP: MAC [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] IP
- DHCP assigns IP configuration to hosts; it does not translate one address form into another.

Answer: DHCP

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are example(s) of stateful application layer protocols?
(i) HTTP
(ii) FTP
(iii) TCP
(iv) POP3
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- HTTP is stateless (each request is independent).
- FTP keeps session state (login, current directory) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stateful.
- TCP is a transport protocol, not application layer.
- POP3 keeps session state (authorization, transaction states) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stateful.

Answer: (ii) and (iv) only
